description_full: Industria de Diseño Textil, S.A., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the retail and online distribution of clothing, footwear, accessories, and household products in Spain, rest of Europe, the Americas, Asia, and internationally. The company sells its products under the Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius, Oysho, Lefties, and Zara Home. It is also involved in the textile manufacturing, logistics, design, insurance, construction, buyer activities, and real estate businesses, as well as provides financial services. Industria de Diseño Textil, S.A. was founded in 1963 and is headquartered in Corunna, Spain.

financial_summary: Industria de Diseno Textil Indi is a mega-cap consumer cyclical business with a $207.8B market cap on $44.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 45% against a 9% cost of capital — a 36-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 58% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $7.3B in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.48× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.5% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 22× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 64% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

own: Insiders own 64.3%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 17%.

people: With about 156,836 employees, each generates about $283K of revenue, 0.7x the Consumer Cyclical median.
That works out to $46K of free cash flow per employee.
